disposition_reason: The only tabulated plant concentrations (Table 1) are for leaf tissue of tomato and zucchini plants, not their edible fruit; edible-crop results (lettuce, basil, tomato fruit) are cumulative metal sums shown only in Figures 2-3 or described as data not shown.

study.design: Field experiments in urban and rural gardens (2011-2013): road distance, pollution source, soil vs soilless, urban vs rural
study.origin: Urban gardens in Bologna (ROAD/10, ROAD/60, RAILWAY/SOIL, RAILWAY/SOILLESS, CENTRE) and a rural control near Medicina, Italy

period.as_reported: 2011 to 2013 (tomato and zucchini 2011; soil vs soilless 2012; tomato, lettuce and basil transplanted April-May 2013)

study.method: Leaves oven-dried <40 C, microwave HNO3/H2O2 digestion, ICP-OES (Spectro Arcos); leaf leaching test for surface deposition
lod: As and Hg below detection limits of 0.01 and 0.02 µg/kg dry weight as printed (p. 1143); other DLs not printed
study.qa: Triplicate samples; CRM 060 (aquatic plants) and CRM 062 (olive leaves) run every 10 samples; CRM 609 for leachates; recoveries not printed

controls.control: Garden 10 m from a main road (ROAD/10)
controls.outcome: Text states heavy metal accumulation about 1.5-fold higher and leaf surface deposition 1.5- to 4-fold higher (zucchini, tomato) at 10 m; per-metal values for edible parts not tabulated
No difference in summed metals for most crops; significant differences only for rosemary and eggplant, driven by zinc; values figure-only
Total metal concentration in tomato fruit not significantly affected by washing (overall mean of summed metals 55.0 ± 2.6 mg/kg dw, data not shown)

unresolved: Table 1 gives leaf-tissue accumulation (mg/kg dw, n not stated) in tomato and zucchini plants at ROAD/10 vs ROAD/60, e.g. tomato leaves Pb 0.28 vs 0.40, Cd 0.20 vs BDL; zucchini leaves Pb 0.16 vs 0.16, Cd BDL; As and Hg BDL. Not recorded as food findings because these are not the edible parts.
Table 2 is deposition on ornamental tree leaves (g/m2), not food.
Lettuce (up to 160 mg/kg dw) and basil (210 mg/kg dw) values in the abstract are cumulative sums of 12 metals read from Fig. 3; not per-metal and not extracted.
Cadmium 0.4-1.2 mg/kg dw in leaves at the rural control is stated as data not shown, not per crop.
Printed As and Hg detection limits (0.01 and 0.02 µg/kg) look implausibly low for ICP-OES; unit may be mg/kg.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: EU maximum levels cited (Regulation 1881/2006 as amended): lead 0.10, 0.30, 0.20 mg/kg fresh weight for legumes, brassica, other vegetables; cadmium 0.05, 0.1, 0.2 mg/kg fw for fruit, stem/root, leaf vegetables
